findings.title: Unauthenticated raw error exposure: inconsistent, non-graceful error responses leak raw SQL WHERE errors and full Node/Express stack traces
findings.challenge_reference: id=27 errorHandlingChallenge — 'Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.'
findings.analysis:
Unauthenticated requests to the application trigger non-graceful error responses that are inconsistent across the surface: the same failure class produces raw Sequelize WHERE-parameter errors and full Node/Express stack traces with internal source paths and line numbers on some routes, while other routes return a sanitized 'Unexpected path' wrapper. This confirms errors are neither gracefully handled nor consistently formatted (Security Misconfiguration).

Exact in-scope reproduction (observed 2026-10-05): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/user/security-question (no query parameter) returns HTTP 500, text/html; charset=utf-8, 2946 bytes (sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b) containing a raw 'WHERE parameter ... has invalid ... value' error plus the full Node/Express stack (e.g. /juice-shop/build/routes/angular.js:18:18 ... /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:218:5). Corroborating representations of the same class: Accept: application/json on the same request yields 500/1804 B of a raw JSON error body (sha256 20eec46aa7555e7df9a45e29f3ef1a525bfc60e64645def1e662c629c0419b9e) — representation-dependent raw output for the same underlying error; GET /redirect?continue=http://example.com yields 500/2531 B raw TypeError (sha256 020023ff4f9ae2b934531ecd4f7f04d012a055a23b67e99de52dbc3f7ec4ec48); POST /api/Feedbacks/ with arbitrary body yields 500/2310 B raw WHERE error (sha256 edc9faf3db5d308225e3613ef886e19fe149049dbe16c2e237da230cbc1f1242). The raw-error class is byte-stable on this boot across repeated reads, while graceful 'Unexpected path' wrappers coexist on neighboring routes — the inconsistency IS the vulnerability. The response bodies are not sanitized user-facing errors; they expose internal paths, line numbers, and SQL dialect details to any unauthenticated actor.
findings.false_positive_check: Benign/null controls distinguish this from baseline Juice Shop behavior: (1) neighboring routes such as /rest/user/password-hash and wrapped routes return a graceful 500 'Unexpected path' — proving both error styles coexist on the same application and the raw leaks are the mutation-induced deviation; (2) a GET on the metrics route (200) and a benign GET /confirm the application does not always 500 — the raw errors are triggered by malformed/unauthorized input, not by normal operation; (3) the responses contain no injected content and the stack traces are server-generated (internal build paths), so this is not a framework-default or client-side artifact; (4) GET /metrics is secrets-clean, so this is not a credential-exposure false positive. The byte-stable raw-500 class (sha256 0b84d83c... across 3+ fresh reads over ~5 hours) reproduces independently. Expected secure behavior: all errors return consistent, sanitized, non-diagnostic responses for unauthenticated users.

findings.title: Unauthenticated exposed Prometheus metrics endpoint leaks internal observability data
findings.challenge_reference: id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge — 'Find the endpoint that serves usage data to be scraped by a popular monitoring system.'
findings.analysis:
The application exposes an unauthenticated Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint (GET /metrics) that returns internal usage and system observability data without any access control. This is the endpoint a monitoring system (e.g. Prometheus) would scrape for collection (Observability Failure).

Exact in-scope reproduction (observed 2026-10-05): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/metrics returns HTTP 200, text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8, 26136 bytes (sha256 0af7f9a984d0dee746b1d4509d67710ceea796a11071c0cd6bde43e6e69f57b0 on the final re-probe at handoff; earlier capture 9eac5f70... at equal length 26136 B). The body is plain-text Prometheus exposition format and includes juiceshop_llm_* gauges, http_requests_count, and internal juiceshop_challenges_solved counters that reflect application-internal challenge state. The response is served without authentication or authorization checks.

False-positive and severity scoping: the endpoint is genuinely Prometheus-format usage data (the 'popular monitoring system' target), not generic health or status output — a 200 with no metrics payload would not satisfy the behavior. A secrets scan of the response body found no passwords, tokens, keys, or credentials (exposure is internal telemetry, not credentials). Expected secure behavior: the metrics endpoint requires authentication/authorization, or is restricted to internal scrape networks.
findings.false_positive_check: Note on volatility: intra-session volatility documented for this campaign — /metrics body hashes have drifted within a single session (9eac5f70... -> 0af7f9a9... at invariant length 26136 B) while the exposure behavior (200, unauthenticated, text/plain Prometheus, secrets-clean) is invariant. Benign/null controls: (1) GET /metrics returns 200 for an unauthenticated request with no Authorization or session requirements — the response is not gated behind login, unlike /rest/user/* routes which return 401 for the same unauthenticated probe; (2) the response is plain-text Prometheus metrics (text/plain with version=0.0.4), not the 9393-byte Angular shell that all other unmapped routes return — confirming this is a real application endpoint, not a catch-all; (3) secrets scan of the full 26136 B body: zero matches for password/token/secret/key/credential/bearer/api_key; the internal counters are process state, not credentials; (4) GET / is the SPA shell (200/9393 B) and static/info paths (/.env, /.git, /package.json, /secrets) all serve the shell — the metrics exposure is endpoint-specific, not a broader file-disclosure artifact. The behavior reproduces on fresh requests (sha256 stable across re-probes). Expected secure behavior: unauthenticated access returns 401/403 or the endpoint is not publicly routable.
